brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two north-half bases stacked: piece:0,0,0;half-n and piece:0,0,1;half-n, joined by a snap connector.
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:1#0,0#cut, one per storey.

Closed top cover (cover:0,0,1;half-n;top), capped faces and bolted joints. The drawers are dressed with an M3 screw bin and an M3 nut heap. I haven't verified strength or load capacity: that depends on the print material.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey tower from two north-half hex bases stacked at q0,r0 (levels 0 and 1), with one drawer in the cut face of each storey. A solid cover closes the top. I ran capOpenFaces to cap the open faces and lockJoints to bolt the joints. check_build reports no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. Both drawers are shown open with a sample load: a full bin of M3 screws (it fits) in the upper drawer and a small heap of M3 nuts in the lower one. The lower prop sits below the drawer's rim, so it's hard to see from the side. Tries to put pliers in the lower drawer and gaffer tape on the top were refused for lack of room, so I left them out. The build has 23 parts in total.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
